notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an average of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice prices indexed to 2015 at 100, currently stands at 132, reflecting a 32% rise over that baseline. This headline increase is relatively recent and uneven across the components. While some commodities have seen sharp gains, others have moved more modestly. The basket provides a broad measure of soft commodity price changes relevant to everyday consumer goods.
notes.movers: Coffee has contributed the most to this rise, up 93% since 2015, followed by orange juice at 22%, while wheat and sugar prices have increased by 7% and 5% respectively. These price shifts largely reflect weather-related disruptions and crop diseases, such as frost and drought impacting arabica coffee regions and citrus greening and hurricanes affecting orange juice supplies. Because these are thin, or less liquid, market commodities, such events can cause pronounced price volatility rather than broad-based inflationary pressures.
notes.why: In summary, a handful of weather-sensitive and disease-affected soft commodities are driving the headline price rise for this basket. Due to the nature of agricultural markets and their exposure to environmental factors, price inputs can remain elevated for multiple years, underscoring the persistent yet uneven risks within these markets.
